title: Nephrology Pharmacology
subtitle: dosing in CKD · RAAS · diuretics · immunosuppression

steps.title: Dose by function, not by creatinine alone
steps.body: Adjust renally cleared drugs using estimated GFR, and use estimated creatinine clearance (Cockcroft-Gault) when labelling is based on CrCl. KDIGO 2024 endorses eGFR equations validated for the population, with cystatin C added where creatinine is unreliable (very low or high muscle mass).
steps.tip: eGFR and Cockcroft-Gault CrCl can differ by more than 30% in the elderly or in oedema — document which one you used.

steps.title: RAAS blockade and hyperkalemia
steps.body: ACEi/ARB reduce intraglomerular pressure and proteinuria, but raise potassium. Manage rather than stop: correct volume, review diuretics, hold NSAIDs, and consider potassium binders, a lower dose, or a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist-based regimen.
steps.tip: A modest creatinine rise (<30%) after starting an ACEi/ARB is expected and is not a reason to stop.

steps.title: Loop diuretics
steps.body: Furosemide acts at the loop of Henle; natriuretic response correlates better with urine chloride than with creatinine. Ceiling doses: furosemide 160-200 mg IV per dose, bumetanide 8-16 mg, torsemide 20-40 mg. In advanced CKD expect modest response, but the goal is decongestion, not natriuresis.
steps.tip: Give IV loop diuretics 1-2 hours before a thiazide to add a sequential nephron block.

steps.title: Transplant immunosuppression
steps.body: Calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus, cyclosporine) inhibit calcineurin/NFAT and cause nephrotoxicity, hypertension, hyperkalemia, and TMA. Antimetabolites (mycophenolate) cause marrow and GI toxicity. mTOR inhibitors cause proteinuria and impaired healing. Belatacept blocks CD80/86 co-stimulation.
steps.tip: CNI troughs are drawn just before the morning dose; a rising creatinine plus rising trough suggests CNI toxicity.

steps.title: Avoid and monitor nephrotoxins
steps.body: Hold NSAIDs, give aminoglycosides only with extended intervals, avoid iodinated contrast when possible, and review PPI, lithium, aminoglycoside, amphotericin, calcineurin inhibitor, and bisphosphonate exposure at every visit.
steps.tip: Sick-day rules: temporarily stop diuretics, RAAS blockers, metformin, and NSAIDs during vomiting, diarrhea, or poor intake.
